                "headline": "Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 15 at 9:16PM CDT until September 15 at 9:45PM CDT by NWS Lincoln IL",
                "description": "At 916 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located near Dunlap, or near\nPeoria, moving east at 25 mph.\n\nHAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to\nroofs, siding, and trees.\n\nThis severe storm will be near...\nPeoria around 920 PM CDT.\nRome around 930 PM CDT.\n\nOther locations impacted by this severe thunderstorm include\nMossville, Kickapoo, and Alta.\n\nThis also includes Rock Island Trail State Park.\n\nThis includes Interstate 74 between mile markers 81 and 82.",
                "instruction": "For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a\nbuilding.\n\nContinuous cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.\nMove indoors immediately. Lightning is one of nature's leading\nkillers. Remember, if you can hear thunder, you are close enough to\nbe struck by lightning.",

                "headline": "Flash Flood Warning issued September 15 at 9:05PM CDT until September 15 at 11:00PM CDT by NWS Lubbock TX",
                "description": "FFWLUB\n\nThe National Weather Service in Lubbock has issued a\n\n* Flash Flood Warning for...\nSouthwestern Castro County in the panhandle of Texas...\nSoutheastern Parmer County in the panhandle of Texas...\n\n* Until 1100 PM CDT.\n\n* At 905 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing\nheavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 3 inches of rain\nhave fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible\nin the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin\nshortly.\n\nHAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,\nhighways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor\ndrainage and low-lying areas.\n\n* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...\nLazbuddie and other areas south of a line from Bovina to Dimmitt.",
                "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nBe especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.",

Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin\nshortly in the advisory area. Between 0.5 and 3 inches of rain\nhave fallen.\n- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 2 inches are expected over\nthe area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.\n- Some locations that will experience flooding include...\nKirksville, Macon, Brookfield, Milan, Unionville, La Plata,\nLancaster, Bevier, Green City, Queen City, Bucklin, Novinger,\nGreentop, Atlanta, Laclede, Downing, Callao, Linneus, Greencastle\nand Brashear.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

                "headline": "Rip Current Statement issued September 15 at 9:01PM CDT until September 17 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Mobile AL",
                "description": "* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents expected.\n\n* WHERE...In Alabama, Mobile Coastal and Baldwin Coastal\nCounties.                 "headline": "Flood Watch issued September 15 at 6:47PM MST until September 16 at 11:00PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ",
                "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...A portion of Southeast Arizona, including the following\nareas, Baboquivari Mountains, Catalina and Rincon Mountains,\nChiricahua Mountains, Dragoon and Mule and Huachuca and Santa Rita\nMountains, Eastern Cochise County below 5000 feet, Galiuro and\nPinaleno Mountains, South Central Pinal County, Southeast Pinal\nCounty, Tohono O'odham Nation, Tucson Metro Area, Upper Gila River\nValley, Upper San Pedro River Valley, Upper Santa Cruz River\nValley/Altar Valley, Western Pima County and White Mountains of\nGraham and Greenlee Counties.\n\n* WHEN...From 11 PM MST this evening through Wednesday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\nCreeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur\nin poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be\nflooded.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Well above normal moisture levels for September are expected to\nresult in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms capable\nof producing heavy rainfall from late tonight through late\ntomorrow night. Rain totals of 1 to 2 inches are expected with\nthe stronger storms with isolated amounts over 2 inches possible.\nAreas that received substantial rainfall over the previous few\ndays will be more susceptible to flash flooding. This rainfall\nwill result in faster response in washes, creeks, and storm\ndrainages.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

                "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by onshore flow restricting Kuskokwim River\ndrainage in combination with excessive rainfall is expected.\n\n* WHERE...Kuskokwim near Bethel.\n\n* WHEN...Until 1000 PM AKDT Tuesday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.\nRiver or stream flows are elevated. Water levels are receding.\nRiver gauge reports indicate rises in water levels from the\nKuskokwim River back-up in combination with heavy rain across the\nadvisory area. This is causing minor flooding from overflow of\npoor drainage areas, especially along the Kuskokwim.\n- Strong onshore winds along the Kuskokwim coast have limited the\nability for the Kuskokwim River to drain out into the Bering Sea.\nThis has caused rapid river rises along the coast and inland into\nBethel. Water levels are expected to back up along Brown Slough\nand flood low lying areas of Bethel and areas along the\nKuskokwim.\n- For Kuskokwim River at Bethel:\nAt 2:50pm the reading was 9.0 feet.\nFlood Stage is 8.5 feet.\n\nImpacts:\nAt 7.0 feet: Action and bankfull stage.\nAt 8.5 feet: Minor flood stage. Water starts to back up along Brown\nSlough and flood low lying areas.\nAt 12.0 feet: Moderate flood stage.\nAt 14.0 feet: Major flood stage.\n\n\n- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

                "description": "* WHAT...Afternoon peak Heat index values from 105 to 109.\n\n* WHERE...For the Four-State area of southern Arkansas, northern\nLouisiana, eastern Texas and southeast Oklahoma.\n\n* WHEN...Until 7 PM CDT Wednesday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and moderate humidity may cause heat\nillnesses.",
                "instruction": "Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of\nthe sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.\n\nTake extra precautions when outside.
